svg.title: rEach and Teach: the whole system on one sheet
svg.desc: A poster combining the system at a glance, the seven guardrail layers, the seven-stage work lifecycle, six reasons the two halves belong together and the privacy split between what is recorded only on assignments, what stays and what leaves.
svg.text: One course, two halves, one closed loop
The student steers. Their own AI agent builds, fenced in by rEach. Teach, the private course server, decides what counts.

g.text: the bounded course partner, inside the agent's harness
Does all the coding, in files, inside the student's slice.
course server · private to the instructors
who is in the course, on which computer
run on the server, never shipped
Author the rules, review the work, record the grade.
Plain words about the business; no
Every write, command and change is

svg.text: Every prompt is refused until the student enrolls on this computer.
No work until the instructors' rules are installed and their signature verifies.
Nothing is submitted without the student's yes, given within 30 minutes for exactly these files.
The agent must prove the slice first.
Each owned file carries an invisible seal and each session leaves a ledger.
Every change is checked against the course's Dovetail shape and the directive table.
Writes and commands land only inside the student's owned files.
course server · private to the instructors
what the course server makes checkable
The roster confirms who is working, on which computer.
Signed by the instructors; unsigned rules stop the work.
Hidden checks run where the agent cannot read them.
Seals and ledgers are read by the server.
A signed receipt says what arrived, and when.
Three failed tries raise a hand to the instructors.
Nothing said before sign-in, in the extracurricular folder or outside the course folder is
The interview profile, private memory, the extracurricular folder, the install's private key.
Leaves, to the course server only
Signed-in assignment conversations, submitted work after a yes, own-part answers, agreed help
The mechanisms behind the glass are private. The guarantees are public. github.com/SteveBenner/rEach
